title: Discrete-time coined quantum walks
summary: A position-and-coin walk with every amplitude calculated through three steps.
why: Explains coherent propagation before graph-search applications.
advantage: No generic advantage from the primitive alone.

title: Continuous-time quantum walks
summary: Derive graph evolution, then solve complete-graph search with a fixed-strength oracle Hamiltonian.
why: Connects graph motion to Hamiltonian simulation and eigenphases.
advantage: Exact complete-graph search in O(√N) continuous oracle time; exponential glued-trees separation cited under a different promise.

title: Szegedy walks and MNRS search
summary: Build two reflections, obtain a stationary reflection, and search with explicit access costs.
why: Unifies quantum-walk search and explains setup/update/check tradeoffs.
advantage: Proven bounded-error oracle-model search bound under reversible-chain access assumptions.

title: Element distinctness
summary: Search six stored subsets for an equal pair, then account for the optimized walk bound.
why: Shows how retained queried data changes query complexity.
advantage: Proven oracle-model O(N^(2/3)) bound; implemented teaching variant has explicit reload cost.
gaps: The elementary subset-amplification algorithm is worked end to end and costs Θ(N) queries. The optimal O(N^(2/3)) theorem is explained through setup/update/gap costs, but its coherent data-retaining subset-walk implementation is not worked through.

title: Triangle finding via Grover search
summary: An explicit four-vertex Grover search with all six adjacency calls counted.
why: Separates an elementary algorithm from graph-structured improved bounds.
advantage: The worked algorithm uses O(n^(3/2)) adjacency queries. Le Gall’s stronger bound is a cited extension, not a taught construction.

title: NAND-tree and formula evaluation
summary: Evaluate a four-leaf NAND formula with an explicit span-program walk, finite phase estimation, and exact measured-error certificate.
why: Represents spectral algorithms for logical formula evaluation.
advantage: Proven query advantages for optimized formula families; complete unoptimized discrete toy circuit uses 84 bit queries versus at most four classically.

title: Quantum backtracking and branch-and-bound
summary: Build a weighted five-node walk, detect zero phase, and extract a verified witness.
why: Connects quantum walks to classical search trees and pruning.
advantage: Proven predicate-test speedup for a specified tree; explicit toy calculation is not a practical speedup.

title: Variational quantum eigensolver
summary: Optimize Z+X on one qubit and derive the actual measurement statistics.
why: Introduces the hybrid variational workflow and its limitations.
advantage: Heuristic for general applications; no general practical speedup established.

title: ADAPT-VQE and adaptive circuits
summary: Measure pool gradients, select a Y rotation, and re-optimize to the exact toy ground state.
why: Shows how measured derivatives can construct an ansatz.
advantage: Heuristic application framework with specific numerical evidence; no general practical speedup.

title: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm
summary: Calculate a one-edge Max-Cut circuit from uniform state to optimal sampled cuts.
why: Makes objective phases, mixing, and sampled optimization explicit.
advantage: Specific theoretical approximation results; general practical advantage unestablished.

title: Imaginary-time evolution and variational alternatives
summary: Compare normalized filtering, a state-dependent unitary, and an exact variational trajectory.
why: Prevents conflation of local QITE, variational imaginary time, and postselected filters.
advantage: Conditional on overlap, ansatz/domain quality, precision and implementation costs.

title: Adiabatic algorithms and quantum annealing
summary: Follow a two-level ground-state path and calculate a finite-time success bound.
why: Distinguishes ideal adiabatic computation from physical annealing.
advantage: Proven guarantees for specified gaps/schedules; no general efficient optimizer.

title: Quantum state tomography
summary: Reconstruct a complex one-qubit density matrix from three measurement bases.
why: Makes full-state output and measurement costs explicit.
advantage: Measurement-estimation task; arbitrary-state output and sample costs grow with dimension.

title: Classical shadows
summary: Derive a randomized Pauli snapshot, its unbiasedness, and its variance.
why: Shows how many observable queries differ from full tomography.
advantage: Proven sample bounds depending on observable norms/locality, accuracy and confidence.

title: Quantum kernel estimation
summary: Estimate overlaps and finish a tiny kernel classification example.
why: Audits quantum feature-map input, sampling, and classical model costs.
advantage: No general practical speedup; depends on feature-map and data assumptions.

title: Variational quantum classifiers
summary: Train a one-parameter classifier and calculate a parameter-shift derivative.
why: Separates trainable-circuit workflows from kernel estimation.
advantage: Heuristic learning workflow; no general practical speedup established.

title: IQP sampling
summary: Calculate a commuting phase circuit and its output distribution.
why: Introduces sampling complexity with a precise error-model boundary.
advantage: Conditional classical-hardness evidence for specified approximation models.

title: Boson and Gaussian boson sampling
summary: Derive photon bunching and Gaussian-input output sectors with a truncation bound.
why: Covers a physically distinct sampling family and permanent/hafnian mechanisms.
advantage: Conditional sampling-hardness evidence; easy toy instances do not establish advantage.

title: Random-circuit sampling
summary: Compute a four-gate distribution and a concrete XEB counterexample.
why: Separates sampling, verification metrics, and application value.
advantage: Conditional complexity evidence; no hardware or useful-application advantage claimed here.

title: Kuperberg hidden-shift sieve
summary: Combine phase qubits and recover all three bits of a modulus-eight hidden shift.
why: Demonstrates coherent postprocessing beyond abelian Fourier sampling.
advantage: Proven subexponential oracle-model time/query bound with storage tradeoffs.

title: Hallgren and Pell-type problems
summary: Construct a reduced-ideal oracle, Fourier-sample its irrational period, and recover a Pell solution.
why: Shows why compact outputs and real-period number theory extend Shor.
advantage: Proven polynomial-time compact-output regulator/Pell algorithm; no proven classical lower bound or practical hardware speedup.

title: Approximating the Jones polynomial
summary: Turn a one-crossing braid into a weighted trace and recover the value one.
why: Adds a topological application with a different output guarantee.
advantage: Proven normalized additive approximation; closure and normalization matter.

title: Quantum Metropolis and Gibbs sampling
summary: Run a coherent thermal proposal, repair rejection by alternating measurements, and calculate the Gibbs output.
why: Covers equilibrium preparation and modern detailed-balance developments.
advantage: Ideal algorithm with explicit mixing and retry costs; no general fast thermalization guarantee.

title: Forrelation and oracle separations
summary: Calculate two-query and genuinely one-indexed-query experiments with explicit error bounds.
why: Shows a separation against randomized classical queries and audits one-query claims.
advantage: Proven oracle-model separation under an explicit promise and bounded-error convention.
